## Findings
- claim-1: Let \(\Lambda=\bigoplus_\lambda\mathbb Zs_\lambda\), \(I_{r,q}:=\bigoplus_{\lambda\nsubseteq q^r}\mathbb Zs_\lambda\), and \(A_{r,q}:=\Lambda/I_{r,q}\). For \(0\le i\le q\), \(0\le j\le r\), define \[ J_{r,q;i,j}:=\bigoplus_{\,i^j\subseteq\lambda\subseteq q^r}\mathbb Z\bar s_\lambda\subseteq A_{r,q}. \] This is an ideal: in every nonzero Littlewood–Richardson term \(s_\lambda s_\nu=\sum_\rho c_{\lambda\nu}^\rho s_\rho\), one has \(\lambda\subseteq\rho\); hence every surviving \(\rho\) still contains \(i^j\). Let \(\omega(s_\lambda)=s_{\lambda'}\). Since \(\lambda\subseteq q^r\iff\lambda'\subseteq r^q\), \(\omega(I_{r,q})=I_{q,r}\), so it induces an integral ring isomorphism \[ \bar\omega_{r,q}:A_{r,q}\xrightarrow{\sim}A_{q,r}, \qquad\bar s_\lambda\mapsto\bar s_{\lambda'}. \] For every \(\lambda\subseteq q^r\), \[ i^j\subseteq\lambda\iff j^i\subseteq\lambda'. \] Indeed, for \(i,j>0\), the left side says \(\lambda_a\ge i\) for \(1\le a\le j\), equivalently \(\lambda'_b=\#\{a:\lambda_a\ge b\}\ge j\) for \(1\le b\le i\), which is \(j^i\subseteq\lambda'\). If \(i=0\) or \(j=0\), both rectangles are empty and the equivalence is vacuous. Thus \(\bar\omega_{r,q}\) maps the displayed \(\mathbb Z\)-basis of \(J_{r,q;i,j}\) bijectively to the displayed \(\mathbb Z\)-basis of \(J_{q,r;j,i}\). Therefore \[ \boxed{\bar\omega_{r,q}(J_{r,q;i,j})=J_{q,r;j,i}}. \] The missing basiswise interval-ideal certificate is established.
## Strategy
Let \(r,q\ge0\), \(0\le i\le q\), \(0\le j\le r\), and
\[
A_{r,q}:=\Lambda/I_{r,q},\qquad
I_{r,q}:=\bigoplus_{\lambda\nsubseteq q^r}\mathbb Zs_\lambda .
\]
Define
\[
J_{r,q;i,j}:=\bigoplus_{i^j\subseteq\lambda\subseteq q^r}\mathbb Z\bar s_\lambda.
\]
This is an ideal: every nonzero LR term in \(s_\lambda s_\nu\) has
\(\lambda\subseteq\rho\); hence each surviving \(\rho\) still contains \(i^j\).

For the Schur involution \(\omega(s_\lambda)=s_{\lambda'}\),
\[
\lambda\subseteq q^r\iff\lambda'\subseteq r^q,
\]
so \(\omega(I_{r,q})=I_{q,r}\), inducing
\[
\bar\omega_{r,q}:A_{r,q}\xrightarrow{\sim}A_{q,r},
\qquad \bar s_\lambda\mapsto\bar s_{\lambda'}.
\]

If \(i,j>0\), then
\[
i^j\subseteq\lambda
\iff \lambda_a\ge i\ (1\le a\le j)
\iff \lambda'_b\ge j\ (1\le b\le i)
\iff j^i\subseteq\lambda'.
\]
If \(i=0\) or \(j=0\), both \(i^j\) and \(j^i\) are empty, so the equivalence is vacuous. This also covers \(r=0\) or \(q=0\), since the index bounds force the relevant rectangle to be empty.

Thus \(\lambda\mapsto\lambda'\) bijects
\[
\{\lambda:i^j\subseteq\lambda\subseteq q^r\}
\quad\text{with}\quad
\{\mu:j^i\subseteq\mu\subseteq r^q\}.
\]
Consequently it bijects the displayed Schur bases, and hence
\[
\boxed{\bar\omega_{r,q}(J_{r,q;i,j})=J_{q,r;j,i}}.
\]

## Gaps
None for this basiswise interval-ideal certificate, relative to the standard Schur involution and Littlewood–Richardson containment.

The missing basiswise proof for the interval ideals is established. Any parent-theorem or minimality argument remains separate.
